book_understanding.teaching_order: A textbook states NDP = GDP - depreciation and then defines depreciation. Here the video first contrasts the words gross and net in plain language, then works a tiny farm example where the 'deduction' is seed, then switches to a factory where the deduction is machine wear (depreciation), takes a side road into why firms like depreciation (tax), comes back to compute gross and net for the factory, and only then writes the NDP and NNP formulas, closing with a boundary rule (business phone vs personal phone). The formula is the conclusion of two worked examples, not the start.
book_understanding.breakdown_rule: Teach the abstract word pair with the smallest possible example, switch to a second example that brings in the real deduction, and only then write the formula and its boundary case.

talmel_summary: The example objects (farmer, sack, machine line, phone) usually appear 1-5 s before the words, and computed values fill waiting chips as they are spoken. The picture shows the step best in the gross-to-net arc labelled '- depreciation', the machine's falling value curve, the expense card set beside the profit card leading to NO TAX, and the YES/NO paths for the two phones. Weak: the profit card arrives long after the profit is spoken, the government card and rule box copy the speech, and the wheat values are not visible on the chips in the sampled frames.

voice.notes: About 172 words per minute, patient and plain. Uses 'maan lijiye' for each new example and 'basically' before definitions. Money is read in Indian units (10 rupees, 1 crore, 30 lakh, 70 lakh) and the arithmetic is said aloud ('100 rupees minus 10 rupees', '10 lakh into 10 rupees'). The tax side-road is told in a slightly excited 'insider' tone. Speech recognition lost about 17 s around 130-147 s and about 10 s around 185-195 s.

game_ideas.player_does: Runs the only ketchup factory in the country for a year: sets how many bottles to make and their price, and watches the machine work.
game_ideas.process_happens: The machine's value bar drops by its depreciation as it runs; at year end the player fills the Gross Produce and Net Produce chips and the system checks them (gross = bottles x price, net = gross - depreciation).
game_ideas.win: Both chips right, and the NDP equation lights with the player's own numbers.
game_ideas.lose: Leaving depreciation out makes net equal gross; the machine's lost value flashes in red beside the chip as the missing deduction.

game_ideas.player_does: Drags items into 'counts for NDP' or 'does not count': factory machine, delivery van, phone used for business, phone used personally, family car, office laptop.
game_ideas.process_happens: Each item travels the YES path into the depreciation column or stops at a crossed NO, as in the video.
game_ideas.lose: Putting the family car in 'counts' shows its NO path, with the note that only assets used to produce goods and services count.
game_ideas.concept: which depreciation counts in NDP and NNP

game_ideas.player_does: As the farmer, decides how much of the harvest to keep back as seed for next season before selling the rest.
game_ideas.process_happens: The sack splits into 'seed kept' and 'available'; the Gross Produce and Net Produce chips fill with the harvest and harvest minus seed.
game_ideas.win: Keep enough seed to repeat the harvest and read off the net produce correctly.
game_ideas.lose: Keeping no seed shows next season's empty field, which teaches why the input must be deducted to see what was truly produced.

checks_learned: Numbers inside one example must agree with each other (a 30% yearly rate does not take 20 years to reach zero); a code check can test rate x years against the stated life.
Every value the voice computes (net 90, net 70 lakh) must appear on its waiting chip at that moment.
A card for a spoken quantity must appear within about 2 s of the first time it is spoken (the profit card came about 25 s late).
Year labels on screen must match the spoken year (the voice puts the 30 lakh drop in 2022, the table shows 70 lakh against 2023).
Flag an aside longer than about 40 s that the target terms do not need; claims about real companies need a source or must be dropped.
The opening and closing checklists must tick exactly the items the voice says are covered.

teaching_best.why: Seed in, harvest out: gross vs net with 10 and 100 before any formal word.
A machine's value curve falling to zero makes depreciation visible as a loss over time.
The formula is drawn as an arc from gross to net labelled '- depreciation' after two worked examples, so it reads as a summary, not a rule to memorise.
Two identical phones with YES and NO paths teach the boundary rule with one everyday object.

teaching_weak.why: 30% a year and about 20 years to scrap do not fit each other; a careful learner will be confused.
About 90 s on tax and a big-company claim; interesting but off the target terms, and the profit card arrives late.
Gross vs net is first given as two text panels with pointer boxes that copy the speech.
The wheat example's net value (90) is spoken but not seen on the Net Produce chip in the sampled frames.
